h: Alice Holt know-how for treetop adventurers
p: The Treetop Challenge isn't something you rush. Allow a good couple of hours or more on the course, plus time for parking, check-in and the safety briefing. Instructors give you a thorough run-through at the start and then watch from the ground, so you'll be clipping yourself on and off as you go. Concentrate during the briefing, because that's where all the important bits are explained.

Younger participants need a participating adult with them, and there are set ratios depending on ages, so check the rules for your group when you book. Footwear with good grip makes a big difference on the wooden platforms, and gloves can help with the ropes.

When it's time to come down to earth, there's plenty around Farnham to enjoy. Frensham Great Pond, a few miles south, is a heathland lake with a sandy shore and lovely walks around the common. Waverley Abbey, near Farnham, was the first Cistercian abbey in England and its atmospheric ruins sit beside the River Wey. Back in Farnham, the Farnham Maltings is a lively arts centre that hosts markets and events, and the castle keep looks down over the town from the hill above Castle Street. For a different kind of woodland, the Bourne Woods, just outside the town, are famous as a filming location for big movies.
